key_insight: Statistical signs of randomness can appear in variational quantum circuits well before trainability is lost, so complexity and barren-plateau behavior are not the same thing.
engineering_relevance: For NISQ circuit design, deeper or more expressive ansätze may still optimize well even when they look random by common complexity diagnostics, so trainability must be checked directly.
method: Studied structured VQAs on the 1D cluster-Ising model and a generalized toric code Hamiltonian.
Measured complexity with Porter-Thomas statistics, entanglement-spectrum level statistics, and inverse participation ratios.
Compared these diagnostics against variational optimization performance as circuit depth increased.
evidence_signal: As depth increased, the circuits moved toward random-state-like or random-matrix-like signatures while optimization remained effective and showed no exponential gradient suppression in the studied regime.
watch_item: The result is depth- and model-dependent: these diagnostics may indicate higher complexity without guaranteeing that the circuit will still avoid barren plateaus at larger scales.
paper_title: Separation of Statistical Complexity and Trainability in Variational Quantum Circuits
